messages:
amal: Heads-up — we need to finalise the KMS rotation procedure for envelope keys next week. scope: AWS KMS + GCP KMS + Azure Key Vault, plus audit/logging and RBAC tweaks. @maria can you confirm the timeline?
maria: Yep. Proposal: automatic rotation every 90 days for root CMKs where provider supports it, but manual rewrap for active envelope keys to avoid downtime.
ryan: Agree on 90d default, but we need a canary rewrap flow for high-throughput models. Suggest: 1% of traffic for 24h, then 10% for 6h, then ramp.
mar ia: (typo) sorry. re: canary, we also need to ensure logs don't leak plaintext key material during rewrap failures. audit logs must record key_alias, rotation_id, outcome, and per-request key_version.
tj: On RBAC — plan to add a new role `kms-rewrap-runner` with only ReEncrypt/Decrypt permissions and no CreateKey/DeleteKey. Use condition-based access: allow rewrap only from our rewrap lambda's principal + on-prem worker principal.
ryan: For AWS specifics: use ReEncrypt API to do envelope rewrap server-side (no plaintext). For GCP, use 'encrypt' with new CMEK key as a second step (we need to draft an idempotent rewrap helper). Azure supports wrapKey/unlock via Key Vault. All rewrap ops must be logged to audit storage (immutable) and routed to SIEM.
amal: Good. What about backwards compatibility for older ciphertext headers? do we version envelope headers?
maria: Yes — embed a small header with schema v1/v2 and key_version. Example header: ```{
  "schema": "env-v2",
  "key_alias": "alias/redwood/app-env",
  "key_version": "2026-03-01-rot1"
}``` Consumers must attempt v2 then fallback to v1 parser.
sre-bot: deploy-check: rewrap-runner lambda passed unit tests, integration tests blocked by missing GCP key alias.
ryan: On rollout timing: schedule low-traffic window (weekend UTC) for full fleet rewrap, but canary steps run during business hours so SRE can watch dashboards. Also include automatic rollback if >1% error rate on decrypts or if p50 latency increases >30ms.
tj: Vulnerability triage note — if a key compromise is suspected, we need an emergency balayage: 1) create emergency key, 2) bulk rewrap all active envelope keys to emergency key (fast path), 3) revoke compromised CMK aliases, 4) audit. That emergency path must be callable by sec-oncall role with MFA gate.
amal: Audit logging: redact plaintext fields, but include non-sensitive metadata: operation, key_alias_from, key_alias_to, principal, request_id, rotation_id. Logs must be forwarded to the SOC cluster and retained for 1 year for SOC2 evidence.
maria: Also add a KMS-integration test that verifies ReEncrypt semantics end-to-end for AWS and equivalent for GCP/Azure nightly. Failure should auto-open a P1 in incidents channel.
ryan: Edge case: partial rewrap where some shards succeed and some fail. Plan: tag records with rewrap_state = pending/retry/complete and have a bounded retry queue. Do not allow reads to fall back to old key if rewrap_state == retry and retry attempts < 3 — instead serve from old key but emit high-severity alert.
sec-oncall: For incident response playbook, add steps: rotate keys, run integrity check on envelope headers, verify audit stream, notify customers per policy. Add a postmortem checklist item: validate that rewrap didn't regress model output (eval sampling).
amal: Ok next actions: (1) maria to author RBAC IAM policies and write sample ReEncrypt commands for each provider, (2) ryan to add canary rollout automation and rollback triggers, (3) tj to update runbooks and emergency path, (4) sec-oncall to draft SOC2 evidence list and alerting thresholds.
maria: I'll push a draft PR with policies + example commands today. ping me if you need IAM snippets. :thumbsup:
amal: thanks — let's sync tomorrow 10am UTC in eng-security to sign off before the weekend.
